Compare ln(x^x) = x·ln(x) with ln(x) directly, since both x^x and x are positive.
x·ln(x) − ln(x) = ln(x)·(x − 1). For 0 < x < 1, ln(x) < 0 and (x − 1) < 0, so their product is positive.
So ln(x^x) > ln(x) for every x in (0,1), meaning x^x > x always. Quantity A is greater.

prompt: In triangle ABC, AB=5, BC=5, AC=6
solutionSteps: Triangle is isosceles with AB = BC = 5, base AC = 6, and angle B between the two equal sides.
Law of Cosines: AC² = AB² + BC² − 2·AB·BC·cos(B) → 36 = 50 − 50cos(B) → cos(B) = 0.28.
B = arccos(0.28) ≈ 73.7°, which is greater than 60°. Quantity A is greater.
